      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4411e162-e402-11f1-9df0-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/Trump-in-Shenzhen-10.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4411e162-e402-11f1-9df0-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/Trump-in-Shenzhen-10.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6f4caf06-e402-11f1-b261-89987c50f799</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:02:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>APEC Summit: Lots of gloss, little real progress?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/apec-summit-lots-of-gloss-little-real-progress</link><description>
Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are holding their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC forum. It is a historic moment in more ways than one, with the leaders of the world’s three most powerful countries around the same table. Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear disarmament and artificial intelligence are all expected to be discussed, and the summit has stoked fears of a carve-up of the world into spheres of influence. But despite the buzz, analysts expect more symbolism than substance, with few concrete breakthroughs likely. Our correspondent in the region has more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/997c2f9a-e3fd-11f1-ad0f-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261119-100153-100636-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/997c2f9a-e3fd-11f1-ad0f-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261119-100153-100636-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9eaaabea-e3fd-11f1-845a-456f10c6396e</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:47:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine's European allies meet in Berlin in show of support</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/ukraine-s-european-allies-meet-in-berlin-in-show-of-support</link><description>
Ukraine’s main European allies are meeting in Berlin on Thursday as a show of support for Kyiv, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner also attending. The gathering, which brings together the leaders of Germany, France, Britain, Poland and Italy as well as NATO chief Mark Rutte, takes place as Trump and Putin meet in China, fuelling fears in Europe that decisions on the war could be made without its input. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Germany has the latest.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3999d8f4-e21b-11f1-8b8b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316805802362.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3999d8f4-e21b-11f1-8b8b-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26316805802362.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b8491ffc-e400-11f1-9722-0f0809d6071d</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:43:58 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:02:37 +0000 en <![CDATA[ What's next for NASA interstellar Voyager 1 probe after passing 1 light-day from Earth? ]]> Voyager 1 has reached a historic milestone in space — it now takes a light-day to send a command to the spacecraft, meaning a full 24 hours for Earth to hail the distant spacecraft.

Since Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched on an initial tour through the outer solar system in 1977, their missions have been packed with science. Voyager 1 looked at Jupiter and Saturn from up close before veering for a flyby of Saturn's moon Titan and Saturn's rings, a pathway that brought it above the plane of the solar system in the early 1980s.

Voyager 1's faster path out of the solar system brought it to one light-day in distance on Wednesday (Nov. 18), while Voyager 2 — which took a slightly slower track to see Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — will reach a light-day of distance in 2035. So what's next for the two Voyager spacecraft as they reach further into interstellar space?

Exploring afar

Interstellar space, which is the area where the sun's constant stream of solar particles within the heliopause gives way to the physics of interstellar space, has been a valuable harvest for both Voyagers. Voyager 1 crossed interstellar space in August 2012 and continues to get data, while Voyager 2 has done the same since November 2018.

"Current science is continuing our investigation on magnetic field strength and direction, plasma density, and energetic particle detection. What is important is to measure how these phenomena change as the spacecraft travels further away from the sun," Suzanne Dodd, project manager for the Voyager missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), told Space.com in an email.

Added to that will be the Voyagers' examinations of plasma and magnetic fields nearby the spacecraft, and a focus on any "solar effects" such as shocks or pressure fronts, added JPL project scientist Linda Spilker in an email.

"Key Voyager science going forward includes observing the extent to which our sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1," Spilker continued. "Where does the sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may last long enough to answer that question."

The team also wants to watch the magnetic field around the spacecraft continue to change direction from the sun, to interstellar space, Spilker noted. That finding was not expected when the Voyagers launched, so scientists are curious to know more — as long as the spacecraft can last, that is.

Power management

Each Voyager continues to lose 4 watts of power a year; their launch power was 470 watts in 1977, and the nuclear power source continues to dwindle, requiring harder choices as the missions approach their 50th years of operations. Instruments have had to be shut off, and both the spacecraft were directed to perform a "Big Bang" of power redistribution earlier this year to preserve as much power as possible without sacrificing science.

Looking forward, Dodd says the team does not anticipate having to make any major changes to spacecraft operations until after the 50th anniversary passes for each spacecraft next August and September (as Voyager 2 launched a few weeks before Voyager 1).

A JPL representative added that the "Big Bang" should keep the remaining science instruments going until that point, although "there is also the thermal state of the spacecraft to balance." The representative added that the margins for power remain "very thin," especially as the spacecraft are quite cold in interstellar space.

"Then there are the things the team can't predict, such as the unexpected loss of contact that happened recently," the spokesperson added, referring to an approximately 48-hour glitch in which Voyager 1 suddenly stopped responding to commands last month — although the spacecraft did quickly recover.

"The goal of the mission is science, so the team is not just concerned with keeping in contact with the Voyagers, but keeping the science instruments going as long as possible," the representative added. "The further away the spacecraft get from Earth, the more they learn about how interstellar space changes further away from the heliopause."

The legacy of Voyager 1

Voyager 1 team members now represent multiple generations of engineers, each one of them with distinct but essential roles. Even the most junior members of the team—Nshan Kazaryan and Bhavana Gupta—are taking on key roles in anticipation of more responsibility in the future, according to JPL mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.

"They have demonstrated their value to the team consistently," Badaruddin said in an email. Kazaryan's responsibilities include negotiating tracking schedules with the Deep Space Network (DSN), a set of three antennas for following distant missions, to keep tabs on the Voyagers. Gupta, meanwhile, has provided documentation to gather important details from the Voyagers' command and control systems to "give detailed instructions" in case of issues.

"One of our most senior team members, Jack Lippincott, has provided critical knowledge and understanding of DSN operations and data interpretation," Badaruddin added. Pointing to one of the DSN antennas in Goldstone, Australia, he said the weather in that region "has been violent the last few weeks, and he has helped us to understand how to deal with unique problems that arose because of it."

While there's no real sense of how much further the spacecraft could keep going, the team says it's committed to be there as long as possible. "It has taken decades of exceptional engineering to get Voyager 1 to the one light-day milestone, and hopefully much further before the mission ends," Dodd said.

Badaruddin added: "One of the reasons that one light-day is so special is that it has never happened before that we were in contact with a spacecraft at this distance, and it may never happen again."

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water ]]>

On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars.

The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago.

MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars. The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result.

Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface, and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place.

Why it mattered

NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind, as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time.

After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014. The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind.

"The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come."

MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study.

NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent, with NASA losing communication with the orbiter.

An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). But when it emerged on the other side, it had gone into an uncontrollable spin that led to a loss of power, dooming the spacecraft.

NASA tried in vain to recover the spacecraft over several months, ultimately declaring the mission over in June 2026.

"Best. Mars. Mission. Ever," Shannon Curry, MAVEN's principal investigator, said of the probe entire 12.5-year mission when it ended. The team "really experienced the loss of a loved one with the end of the mission here."

]]> <![CDATA[ Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why ]]> More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished.

Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past.

Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth.

Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years.

But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged.

One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity.

It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years.

"Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement.

"The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance."

What erased the geological record?

In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame.

Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years.

The results suggest that three major ancient continental regions (Laurentia (modern North America), Baltica (northern Europe) and North China were gradually pushed up during the Neoproterozoic Era, approximately one billion to 540 million years ago.

This would have left vast areas of land exposed to weathering and erosion for long periods, allowing water, wind and other processes to wear away rock that had formed much earlier.

But removing the rock is only part of the puzzle. They also needed to explain why the gaps are still visible today.

Their models suggest that the same regions subsequently began to sink. As sea levels rose relative to the land, sediment accumulated over the older, eroded surfaces, creating the sharp divide between ancient and younger rocks that we can still see today.

Crucially, the researchers found that the timing of the simulated continental uplift and sinking was consistent with geological evidence from North America, northern Europe and North China. This suggests that movements deep within Earth's mantle may have played a major role in shaping the geological record we see today.

On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit.

In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket? ]]> The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket.

NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet.

But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the "Mars Czar") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'"

Shotgun marriage?

Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform.

Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed.

"The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad."

Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration.

Lemonade squeeze

However, Hubbard said he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade."

It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration.

"SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. "Nuclear Electric Propulsion [NEP] is of little value in traveling to Mars, not shaving any time off the transit. The real value of NEP is for risk reduction, use at the moon, outer planets and even bolder ideas like interstellar travel," Hubbard concluded.

Resolution gap

"This, by far, is the shortest Mars mission ever conceived of," said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif., speaking Nov. 10 during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

Kick-started by NASA in March 2026, the SkyFall project has grown from roughly six people to over 200 individuals who are now working on the initiative, said Golombek. "This is an incredibly rapid development and build," he said.

"It's really to demonstrate that exploration is possible with helicopters … filling what I call a 'resolution gap' between orbital information and surface information," Golombek told the MEPAG.

Once deployed by a helicopter deployment system, the threesome will spin up their rotors at about a kilometer above the surface of Mars. Then each helicopter lands on its own, ready to undertake flights every other solar day on the Red Planet. On average, a day (labeled as a sol) on Mars lasts 24 hours 39 minutes 35 seconds, from one noon to the next.

SkyFall's prime mission is six months, with a one-year goal," Golombek said, and the intent is to arrive in northern spring on Mars, a time where the vehicles are unlikely to encounter dust storms.

On the to-do list of NASA level one science requisites are for the helicopters to capture high-resolution imagery, perform a set scientific tasks, and help to prepare for future human exploration of Mars, said Golombek.

From their initial landing spots, the whirlybirds could potentially go tens to 100's of kilometers or more in different directions. Identical for all three helicopters, the nominal payload consists of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras.

That gear can examine the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the planet's radiation environment.

"The real star of the show is ground penetrating radar [GPR] with a flexible antenna," Golombek noted. That ultra-small GPR hardware can look for buried rocks, the layering of the Mars home turf, as well as spot subsurface ice deposits.

]]> <![CDATA[ Supernova explodes before astronomers' eyes | Space photo of the day for Nov. 18, 2026 ]]>

A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth.

What is it?

Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf.

During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion.

Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter.

This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place.

Why is it incredible?

Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres.

ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system.

But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova.

Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.

]]> <![CDATA[ The Lego Star Trek bridge diorama set should be your gateway to finally watching the Original Series ]]> It's not quite a five-year mission, but as Star Trek celebrated its 60th anniversary in September of this year (we may have mentioned it once or twice), I decided it was high time I finally watched the original Star Trek.

Before this year, I hadn't seen a single episode of "Star Trek: The Original Series", as it's now known. I'm a millennial; I grew up on "The Next Generation", "Deep Space Nine" and "Voyager". By comparison, the old series (TOS) always looked so… old and naff whenever I saw clips of it.

But now I have seen the original series. Over the course of 2026, I've ploughed through all 79 episodes, spread across three seasons. And you know what? It's pretty damn good. Even with the shiny 2006 remasters, you'll have to prepare yourself for some bad special effects work, but the scripts are interesting, the sci-fi concepts are out there, and the acting — especially from Shatner and Nimoy — is top-notch.

And just as I finally discovered a love for this classic sci-fi series, what should drop into my lap? Why it's the new Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge diorama set from Lego. Now I have more on my wishlist to add to the Best lego space sets.

Boldly building where no one has built before

Let's start with the Band-Aid rip: this set is $200. I know; it stings, especially when Star Trek promised us a future where money doesn't exist. But at 1701 pieces (nice, I see what you did there), it's much better value from a bricks-per-dollar perspective than the X-Files set we checked out recently.

Still, that's no small investment for a toy, even if it will make a lovely display piece when it's built.

As the name suggests, you get a full Lego-ified recreation of the bridge of the USS Enterprise (NCC-1701, no A, B, C, or D). This includes Captain Kirk's chair, the helm positions ahead of him (manned by Chekov and Sulu), and all of the surrounding computer displays where you usually find Spock, Uhura and Scotty.

There's even a viewscreen that can sit in front of the crew, displaying an adorable Klingon commander facing off against Kirk.

Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge: $199.99
Board the legendary starship and meet the crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 for an amazing building experience. Recreate the iconic bridge and transporter room that served as the backdrop for epic scenes from "Star Trek: The Original Series".View Deal

Alongside the main bridge, there are a few fun extras bolted on, including a rotating transporter pad (which can make minifigures "disappear") and a working turbolift door connected to the back of the main bridge diorama. You'll have to make the swoosh sound effect yourself, though.

It's a wonderfully faithful recreation of Kirk's command center, complete with computer panels and screens, swiveling chairs and that weird scope thing that Spock was always looking into.

That said, it's a little lacking in proper Easter eggs. There are some tribbles hiding around the build, and the monitors have custom stickers showing cool Trekkie things. The weapon display racks on the back hold an array of pointy Klingon blades, Starfleet phasers, Sulu's fencing rapier and even Spock's harp, but compared to, say, the X-Files set we built recently, it feels a bit lacking in those deep-cut references.

Helping Star Trek live long and prosper

All in all, it's a fantastic little diorama, but when it was announced, I'll admit I was a little puzzled as to who it was aimed at. "Star Trek fans, duh!" is the obvious response, but the Venn diagram crossover between "people who are nostalgic for the original series of Star Trek" and "people who want to buy $200 Lego sets" has to be pretty small, right?

Star Trek first aired way back in 1966, which means the first generation of fans are now 70 years old and upwards. Lord knows I hope I'm still building Lego sets when I'm 70, but is that a large enough crowd to make this set a success? Then again the show was repeated and syndicated throughout the 70s and 80s, which means hopefully there'll be some younger buyers, too.

The playset aspects of the set are even more puzzling. The working door, exploding monitor and spinning transporter pad are great additions to a kids' playset, but this isn't that — it's a display for nostalgic Star Trek fans. The design of the set just feels a bit confused.

But then it hit me. Maybe this isn't just for fans of the original series; maybe it's meant to create some new fans. I started watching the original Star Trek 60 years after its debut because… well, I'm the sci-fi editor for a space website, and it felt wrong that I hadn't seen it. But most people don't have that sort of professional impetus. The average person won't jump back to watch a 60-year-old TV show without a polite nudge, and this set does a great job of highlighting the charm and optimism of Star Trek's debut outing.

I don't know, maybe I'm just projecting here. Maybe Lego bought the rights to make Star Trek sets and needed something to do after they'd mined all the nostalgia they could from the excellent Enterprise D set they released in 2025. Maybe this is just a toy for big kids.

Or maybe… just maybe, it's meant to inspire the next generation of Star Trek fans to check out where the magic started.

Disclaimer: We were sent a copy of the Star Trek: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701 Bridge set by Lego.

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/trump-se-v-cine-sesel-s-putinem-muze-z-toho-vzejit-spousta-uzasnych-veci-rekl_2611190701_ako</link>
 <description>Americký prezident Donald Trump se ve čtvrtek sešel se svým ruským protějškem Vladimirem Putinem na okraj summitu Asijsko-pacifického hospodářského společenství v Číně, píší tiskové agentury. Ze schůzky může vzejít spousta úžasných věcí, prohlásil Trump na úvod jejich prvního setkání od loňského srpna. Jednání trvalo zhruba 40 minut, napsala agentura AP.</description>

 <title>ONLINE: Ukrajinci znovu cílili na Krymský most. Železniční doprava se kvůli útoku zastavila</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/krymsky-most-aktualne-dnes-utok-2026-ukrajina-rusko-online-valka_2611190612_ako</link>
 <description>Na Krymském mostě byl po dalším ukrajinském útoku přerušen provoz vlaků, oznámilo ve čtvrtek podle ruské služby BBC ministerstvo dopravy v Moskvě. Kyjev aktuální úder potvrdil. Ukrajina na most, který přes Kerčský průliv spojuje ruskou pevninu s Krymem, zaútočila již v úterý a vážně ho poškodila. Po úterním úderu na něm byla zastavena automobilová doprava.</description>

<item>
 <title>Konečně je sečteno, demokraté získají v Senátu 56 křesel. Ve sněmovně hledají na Trumpa ‚ostříleného právníka‘</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/konecne-je-secteno-demokrate-ziskaji-v-senatu-56-kresel-ve-snemovne-hledaji-na_2611190500_vdv</link>
 <description>Dva týdny po amerických volbách jsou známy výsledky z Aljašky, kde Demokratická strana získala 56. křeslo v Senátu a v horní komoře Kongresu má nejsilnější mandát od roku 1958. Dalším krokem pro demokraty je zvolit si vedení, které příští dva roky povede opozici vůči Bílému domu. Stávající předseda Chuck Schumer tvrdí, že už teď má mezi spolustraníky dost hlasů. Prosincová volba předsedy však bude tajná a Schumer je nepopulární.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-24t022637z_1_261016-172700_vdv.JPG?itok=Vc_wN72Y" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 05:00:00 +0100</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Deportační centrum ve Rwandě? Unijní státy se vrhají do slepé uličky jako Británie, míní Magda Faltová</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/deportacni-centrum-ve-rwande-unijni-staty-se-vrhaji-do-slepe-ulicky-jako_2611190010_cen</link>
 <description>Pět evropských zemí chce neúspěšné žadatele o azyl posílat do Rwandy. Jaký efekt může přinést zřízení deportačního centra v této africké zemi? Může fungovat jako odstrašení příchozích? „Státy o tom často mluví, ale čísla, data a výzkumy to nepotvrzují,“ říká pro Radiožurnál Magda Faltová, ředitelka Sdružení pro integraci a migraci. Co zavádí přísnější migrační politika EU? A měla by být tvrdší také pravidla pro slučování rodin uprchlíků?</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/717368232979ac4c18bb8f9665af9e9c.jpg?itok=Isbm-cqw" type="image/jpeg" />

 <title>Skryté kamery i AI. Jižní Korea se snaží zabránit podvodům u důležitých přijímaček na vysoké školy</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/skryte-kamery-i-ai-jizni-korea-se-snazi-zabranit-podvodum-u-dulezitych_2611182332_ntu</link>
 <description>Jihokorejské úřady se snaží zabránit podvádění při celostátní přijímací zkoušce na vysoké školy. Narůstají obavy, že umělá inteligence a chytrá zařízení způsobí odhalování podvodů ještě obtížnějším.</description>

</item>

 <title>BONUS: Amerikou obchází ‚strašidlo socialismu‘. Pro jedny hrozba, pro druhé naděje na změnu</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/bonus-amerikou-obchazi-strasidlo-socialismu-pro-jedny-hrozba-pro-druhe-nadeje-na_2611182250_ntu</link>
 <description>Socialismus a komunismus jsou ve Spojených státech dlouhodobě vykreslovány jako hrozba. Zatímco část Američanů si pod těmito pojmy představuje ztrátu svobody a státní útlak, jinou část americké společnosti oslovují myšlenky demokratického socialismu, s nimiž přichází část americké levice. Proč mají Američané o socialismu tak rozdílné představy? Poslechněte si bonusovou epizodu podcastu Přes Atlantik.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Spor o vedení polského ústavního soudu pokračuje. Instituce teď zbavila imunity dosavadního předsedu</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/spor-o-vedeni-polskeho-ustavniho-soudu-pokracuje-instituce-ted-zbavila-imunity_2611182208_ntu</link>
 <description>Valné shromáždění soudců polského ústavního soudu ve středu zbavilo imunity muže, kterého polská opozice považuje za předsedu tohoto soudu, píše agentura Reuters. Na konci října ústavní soud oznámil, že jeho nejdéle sloužící soudkyně Anna Korwinová-Piotrowská pozastavila výkon funkce předsedovi Bogdanu Świenczkowskému a že vedení soudu se ujímá ona. </description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-31t092540z_1_261118-214606_ntu.JPG?itok=0fkHljro" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>V Amazonii vyfotili po desetiletích členy izolovaně žijícího kmene Awá, z pralesa vyšli pro jídlo</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/v-amazonii-vyfotili-po-desetiletich-cleny-izolovane-zijiciho-kmene-awa-z-pralesa_2611181754_cen</link>
 <description>Nevládní organizace Survival International v úterý zveřejnila snímky skupiny z domorodého kmene z brazilské Amazonie, který žije izolovaně v deštném pralese. Asi 20 jeho členů se podařilo vyfotografovat poprvé po zhruba 30 letech, když sami vyšli požádat sousední kmen o jídlo, informovaly ve středu deník El País a agentura AP.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-11-17t235319z_7_261118-174841_cen.JPG?itok=7ARJdQph" type="image/jpeg" />

<item>
 <title>Rusové měli Krymský most velmi dobře zabezpečený. Přesto ho nedokázali ubránit, popisuje generál Macko</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/rusove-meli-krymsky-most-velmi-dobre-zabezpeceny-presto-ho-nedokazali-ubranit_2611181705_jho</link>
 <description>Den poté, co Ukrajina zasáhla Krymský most, se na něm obnovila železniční doprava. Do průlivu se ale zřítil masivní silniční oblouk, který pomáhal zajistit stabilitu celé konstrukce. Do moře byl stržený i 200metrový úsek asfaltu silnice. Auta tak musí využívat trajekty nebo Azovské moře objíždět po pevnině. „Ukrajinci museli velmi náročně plánovat. Systém přesytili množstvím prostředků,“ říká pro Radiožurnál generálporučík v záloze Pavel Macko.</description>

<description>Českým internetem dnes protekl rekordní počet dat. A ne být na hráče po sestupu do béčka Ligy národů hrdý</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906140-tohle-je-malo-mel-by-rict-denia-a-ne-byt-na-hrace-po-sestupu-do-becka-ligy-narodu-hrdy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906140-tohle-je-malo-mel-by-rict-denia-a-ne-byt-na-hrace-po-sestupu-do-becka-ligy-narodu-hrdy.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:54:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Pavel Hartman</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Šest porážek v řadě, děsivé skóre 3:14, jednoznačný sestup z áčka do béčka Ligy národů. A hlavní trenér národního mužstva pronese, že je na hráče hrdý.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký kraj přispěje na střechu chráněné sokolovny v Jablonci</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906116-liberecky-kraj-prispeje-na-strechu-chranene-sokolovny-v-jablonci-nad-nisou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906116-liberecky-kraj-prispeje-na-strechu-chranene-sokolovny-v-jablonci-nad-nisou.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 06:54:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj přispěje půl milionem korun na obnovu střechy sokolovny v Jablonci nad Nisou. Do památkově chráněné budovy zatéká a opravu nutně potřebuje, řekla mluvčí Libereckého kraje Pavla Sýkorová.</description></item><item><title>Do jabloneckých zahrad zamířilo 160 jabloní starých odrůd. K výročí města</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905921-do-jabloneckych-zahrad-zamirilo-160-jabloni-starych-odrud-k-vyroci-mesta.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905921-do-jabloneckych-zahrad-zamirilo-160-jabloni-starych-odrud-k-vyroci-mesta.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Jablonec nad Nisou rozdal v uplynulých dnech obyvatelům 160 sazenic tradičních odrůd jabloní, každou za symbolickou cenu 160 korun. Projekt připomínající 160 let od povýšení Jablonce na město má vrátit odolné stromy zpět do místních zahrad.</description></item><item><title>Auto se u Spálova zřítilo ze srázu, těžce zraněnou řidičku vyprostili hasiči</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906118-auto-se-u-spalova-zritilo-ze-srazu-tezce-zranenou-ridicku-vyprostili-hasici.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906118-auto-se-u-spalova-zritilo-ze-srazu-tezce-zranenou-ridicku-vyprostili-hasici.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 19:01:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>K vážné nehodě došlo ve středu odpoledne na Semilsku. Řidička zůstala ve voze zaklíněná, zranil se i spolujezdec.</description></item><item><title>Předvánoční nákupy lákají i kyberzločince. Podvodům čelila většina Čechů, varují experti</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906061-predvanocni-nakupy-lakaji-i-kyberzlocince-podvodum-celila-vetsina-cechu-varuji-experti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906061-predvanocni-nakupy-lakaji-i-kyberzlocince-podvodum-celila-vetsina-cechu-varuji-experti.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 18:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Michael Daněk</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>S blížícími se Vánocemi a slevovými akcemi Black Friday roste také riziko internetových podvodů. S některou formou kybernetického útoku se v posledních 12 měsících setkalo 62 procent dospělých Čechů. Nejčastěji šlo o spamové nabídky, následovaly podvodné e-maily. Vyplývá to z aktuálního výzkumu.</description></item><item><title>Tomáš Arsov zavítá s Rossmann Tour do Liberce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905700-tomas-arsov-zavita-s-rossmann-tour-do-liberce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905700-tomas-arsov-zavita-s-rossmann-tour-do-liberce.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:55:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Tomáš Arsov zamíří ve středu 25. listopadu 2026 do Liberce. Vstup je zdarma a bez registrace.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký Strom přání slaví dvacet let. Několik vylosovaných šťastlivců se dočká splnění svého snu v lednu na radnici.</description></item><item><title>Nečekejte na první sníh. Do hor vyrazte na zimních pneumatikách</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905933-necekejte-na-prvni-snih-do-hor-vyrazte-na-zimnich-pneumatikach.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905933-necekejte-na-prvni-snih-do-hor-vyrazte-na-zimnich-pneumatikach.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:02:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Zimní výbava není jen otázkou pneumatik. Některé úseky v Libereckém kraji navíc vyžadují zimní pneumatiky bez ohledu na aktuální počasí.</description></item></channel></rss>
